panel.introduction: Sedna follows an exceptionally distant, elongated orbit beyond the planetary region. This grid-covered illustration conveys its thermal size estimate; its actual shape and surface terrain remain unresolved.

facts.label: Rotation
facts.value: About 10.3 hours from photometry; aliases and a possible doubled shape period remain unresolved.

moreFacts.label: Shape interpretation
moreFacts.value: Size-constrained spherical illustration at the 995 ±80 km thermal diameter. Herschel constrains effective size, not three axes; no resolved global shape or topography is represented.

controls.label: Shape model
controls.description: Size-constrained spherical illustration at the 995 ±80 km thermal diameter. Herschel constrains effective size, not three axes; no resolved global shape or topography is represented. Illustrative ICRF north pole (RA 0°, Dec +90°), arbitrary prime meridian and phase. No measured body pole or absolute surface attitude is claimed. The grid marks unmapped terrain.
controls.title: Published size model; shape unresolved

resources.label: Shape source
resources.description: Pál et al. (2012), Herschel/PACS thermophysical analysis; Gaudi et al. (2005), rotational photometry.
